mentions.name: PhotoGather
mentions.description: iPhone app that virtually stitches a user's entire photo library into one navigable gigapixel image with pinch-and-zoom. On import it hierarchically groups photos by date and similarity, and users can edit groups, change the layout, and adjust photo sizes. Under the hood it finds the best-sized rectangle to fit arbitrary numbers of thumbnails with different aspect ratios (enabling recursive stitching into rectangular group thumbnails) and drives the pinch/zoom UI directly from nested thumbnails without slicing into fixed-size tiles. Curating the library also surfaces forgotten memories and moments.
mentions.problem: The author had 40k+ photos on an iPhone and wanted a better way to interact with and organize such a large photo library.
